headline: Sensex and Nifty fall as Indian markets face eighth straight weekly loss amid surging US Treasury yields

marketStatus.message: Market is open for trading today.

why: US 10-year Treasury yields surged to 5.31%, the highest level since 2007, impacting global sentiment
Auto and metal sectors are acting as the primary draggers in today's trading session
Global rate hikes and rising oil prices have sparked significant outflows from Indian benchmarks
The Indian stock market is currently on track for its longest weekly losing run in 25 years
whatHappening: The Sensex dropped 400 points while the Nifty 50 slipped below the 22,500 mark during intraday trade
GST collections grew 14.7% to over ₹2.03 lakh crore in September 2026, a significant fiscal milestone
India's manufacturing PMI reached a seven-month high in September 2026 driven by strong demand
Industrial growth quickened to 8% in August 2026 following a broad-based uptick across sectors
summary: Indian markets are trading lower with the Nifty slipping below 22,500, marking a potential eighth consecutive weekly loss. Despite strong domestic data like record GST collections and high manufacturing PMI, surging US yields are weighing heavily on sentiment. Auto and metal stocks are among the primary laggards in today's volatile session.
